documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 y/o woman transferring care. Teaches ballet to kids and adults at a local studio.

Hx: anorexia nervosa as a teenager, did outpatient treatment, in remission for several years. Eats regularly now, no restricting or purging, no compensatory exercise beyond teaching. Weight has been steady around where it is today and she is comfortable with it. Depression in her late teens/early 20s, on sertraline 50 mg for years with good effect, prior PCP prescribed. Takes vitamin D 2000 units daily. Periods regular, roughly monthly. Not sexually active.

Allergies: latex, sulfa drugs. She does not remember the reactions, both on her old list.
Family: mother breast cancer at 51. Maternal grandmother ovarian cancer at 47. Her sister carries a BRCA1 mutation.
Social: never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Lives locally.
Surgeries: none.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: thin, well appearing. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lanugo or calluses on the knuckles. Mood euthymic, affect full.

PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Major depressive disorder, stable on sertraline 50. Continue, I'll take over refills.
2. Anorexia nervosa, in remission. Weight steady, BMI on the low side but stable for her. Will track weight at visits without making a production of it; she prefers not to see the number and we'll respect that.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP today. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap was done at the prior office last year per her report, will confirm with records. Flu shot in October.

Records requested. Return for a physical in about a year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/03/2022
Reason for referral: amenorrhea

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Ms. Gutman, 24, who has now gone about five months without a period after years of regular monthly cycles. She reports no meaningful change in weight, and no nipple discharge or excess hair growth. She has not been sexually active and has had no pregnancies. Background includes anorexia nervosa, now in remission, and depression treated with sertraline 50 mg daily; she also takes vitamin D 2000 units daily. Allergic to latex and sulfa drugs. Her mother had breast cancer at 51, her maternal grandmother ovarian cancer at 47, and a sister carries a BRCA1 mutation. Never smoker, no alcohol; she teaches ballet.

On exam, blood pressure 120/78 and pulse 72. Thyroid without enlargement or nodularity. The remainder of the general and pelvic examination was normal.

Results: urine pregnancy test negative. Prolactin 18 ng/mL (ref 4-23). TSH 2.5 mIU/L (ref 0.4-4.0). FSH 85 mIU/mL, well above the follicular-phase range of 3.5-12.5.

Impression: secondary amenorrhea with a markedly elevated FSH, i.e. hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Normal prolactin and thyroid function. This pattern points toward primary ovarian insufficiency, which I will confirm with a repeat FSH in about four weeks before we talk about treatment.

Plan: repeat FSH in 4 weeks with a follow-up visit to review. We discussed what the diagnosis would mean.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

medications.drug_text: estradiol 1 MG / norethindrone acetate 0.5 MG Oral Tablet

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 06/07/2022

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Gutman returned to review her repeat FSH, which is 78 mIU/mL, again in the menopausal range and consistent with the May value. With six months of amenorrhea and two elevated FSH levels, the diagnosis is primary ovarian insufficiency.

We spent most of the visit on what this means for her: bone and heart health, the need for hormone replacement until the usual age of menopause, and fertility, which is markedly reduced though occasional spontaneous ovulation does happen. She took it in thoughtfully.

Plan: started estradiol 1 mg / norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg, one tablet daily. Continue vitamin D. Follow up with me yearly or sooner with concerns.

Allergies: latex, sulfa.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Question about hormone pills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, gyn started me on hormone replacement for the ovarian insufficiency. With my mom's breast cancer, is this safe for me? Should I be worried?

documents.title: RE: Question about hormone pills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. The breast cancer concerns people hear about come from studies of women in their 50s and 60s taking hormones after natural menopause. For a young woman whose ovaries have stopped early, the replacement is giving back roughly what your body would be making anyway, and skipping it carries real risks to your bones and heart. Your gynecologist's plan is the standard one and I agree with it. We'll keep an eye on breast screening because of your mom's history when the time comes.

documents.title: Positive test??
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I took a home pregnancy test this morning and it's positive. Two of them actually. My last bleed was around June 2. I thought this basically couldn't happen with my ovaries? What do I do with the hormone pills and the sertraline?

documents.title: RE: Positive test??
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations if this is happy news, and I know it's a surprise either way. Ovarian insufficiency makes pregnancy uncommon but not impossible; the ovaries can still release an egg now and then. Please stop the estradiol/norethindrone now. Keep taking sertraline 50 mg: it is one of the better-studied antidepressants in pregnancy, and stopping it suddenly carries its own risks for you. Keep the vitamin D too. I've put in a referral to obstetrics, and our nurse will call you today to help with scheduling and answer questions.

No bleeding or cramping. OB intake booked; she will call the OB office back to confirm the time. Told to call for bleeding, pain, or if she is unable to keep food down. She asked that weights at OB be done facing away from the scale; encouraged her to tell them.

OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT SUMMARY
Visit date: 12/15/2023
Patient: Deborah Gutman, 26, G1P0, 28w0d by early ultrasound (LMP approx 06/02/2023)
Copy to primary care

Subjective: Feels well overall. Her main worry today is that she hasn't put on much weight: 4 kg since early pregnancy. She has a history of anorexia nervosa and says things have been steadier over the past year; prepregnancy BMI was 17. Spontaneous conception despite her known primary ovarian insufficiency.

Medications: sertraline 50 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily; estradiol/norethindrone - ON HOLD since positive test.
Allergies: latex, sulfa drugs.
Family history: mother breast cancer 51; maternal grandmother ovarian cancer 47; sister BRCA1 carrier.

Objective: Wt 50 kg, Ht 165 cm, BP 110/70. Fundal height 24 cm, lagging for dates. FHT normal.
Labs today: Hgb 11.2 g/dL, Hct 33%, WBC 9,000/mm3, platelets 250,000/mm3. Urinalysis normal.
Growth ultrasound today: single live intrauterine pregnancy; estimated fetal weight at the 7th percentile; amniotic fluid volume normal.

Assessment: 28 weeks with intrauterine growth restriction, in the setting of low maternal weight and limited gain.
Plan: Tdap given today. Nutrition referral; she is open to it. Serial growth scans and closer antenatal visits. Reviewed fetal movement counting and when to call.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics

BIRTHING CENTER, COMMUNITY HOSPITAL - MATERNAL DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 01/26/2024  Discharge: 01/28/2024

Admission diagnosis: preterm labor at 34w0d; pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction.
Discharge diagnosis: spontaneous preterm vaginal delivery at 34w0d.

Course: Presented in spontaneous labor with regular contractions and cervical change; membranes intact on arrival. Progressed without augmentation to an uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery. Infant small for gestational age, admitted to the special care nursery for prematurity; mother visiting and pumping. Estimated blood loss within normal limits. Postpartum course uneventful.

Medications at discharge: sertraline 50 mg daily (continue); vitamin D3 2000 units daily. Hormone therapy remains on hold until the postpartum visit.
Allergies: latex (latex-free precautions observed), sulfonamides.

Follow-up: postpartum visit with obstetrics in about 6 weeks; primary care as scheduled. Return precautions reviewed, including mood symptoms.

documents.title: Gynecology visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - VISIT NOTE
Date of service: 10/22/2025

Deborah is 28 and came for her annual visit with a month of bloating that has been building gradually, getting full after small meals, and more fatigue than usual, which she had chalked up to work. Her clothes are tight at the waist. On hormone therapy her bleeding has been irregular with occasional skipped bleeds, and she has had none for close to two months. She is sexually active and not using contraception. No weight loss, no fever, no blood in the stool or black stools.

History: primary ovarian insufficiency diagnosed 2022; anorexia nervosa in remission; depression on sertraline; one pregnancy with fetal growth restriction, delivered preterm at 34 weeks in January 2024.
Medications: estradiol 1 mg/norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.
Family history: mother breast cancer at 51; maternal grandmother ovarian cancer at 47; sister BRCA1 carrier.

Exam: abdomen distended but soft; a firm, mobile mass is palpable in the lower abdomen. Pelvic exam: right adnexal mass.

Studies: serum alpha-fetoprotein and beta-hCG both elevated. Transvaginal ultrasound in the office shows a large heterogeneous right ovarian mass with areas of necrosis and hemorrhage, and no intrauterine pregnancy.

Assessment: complex right ovarian mass, concerning for malignancy.
Plan: urgent referral to gynecologic oncology, who will arrange CA-125 and staging imaging. Discussed with Deborah in detail; she has my direct line.

Gynecology

documents.title: PCP call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Deborah after receiving the gyn note. She knows the mass is suspicious. Gyn onc appointment Thursday, blood work and CT Wednesday. Scared, but has her partner and her mother helping with the baby. Sleeping poorly. No pain, eating small amounts. We talked through what to expect at the consult. Continue sertraline. She'll message after the visit; told her to call any time.

reports.text: CT of the chest with intravenous contrast. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No pleural or pericardial effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with oral and intravenous contrast. Complex solid and cystic right adnexal mass measuring about 13.5 cm in greatest dimension, displacing bowel superiorly. No ascites. No peritoneal or omental nodularity. No retroperitoneal or pelvic lymphadenopathy. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys normal. Uterus normal. No hydronephrosis. Bowel without obstruction.
reports.conclusion: Large complex right adnexal mass. No ascites, lymphadenopathy, peritoneal disease or distant spread.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology consultation
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 10/30/2025
Referred by: outside gynecology; copy to primary care

28-year-old with primary ovarian insufficiency on hormone therapy, depression, and anorexia nervosa in remission, referred for a large right ovarian mass. Symptoms: about a month of bloating, early satiety and fatigue. AFP and beta-hCG were reported elevated at the referring office.

CA-125 on 10/29: 212 U/mL.
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 10/29: complex right adnexal mass about 13.5 cm; no ascites, adenopathy, peritoneal or distant disease.

Exam: thin, well appearing. Abdomen soft, mildly distended; firm mobile mass rising out of the pelvis. No lymphadenopathy.

Assessment: large right adnexal mass, imaging suggesting disease confined to the pelvis. The marker pattern raises a germ cell tumor alongside an epithelial cancer; pathology will decide.
Plan: exploratory laparotomy with frozen section and full surgical staging. Given primary ovarian insufficiency and the family history, she does not wish to preserve the uterus or the opposite ovary if the frozen section shows an epithelial cancer; consented accordingly. Germline genetic testing to follow the pathology. Surgery booked for 11/06.

Allergies: LATEX, sulfa - latex-safe OR.

Gynecologic Oncology

conditions.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma of ovary
conditions.note: high-grade serous, right ovary, FIGO IC1

medications.drug_text: estradiol 1 MG / norethindrone acetate 0.5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.reason: hysterectomy and oophorectomy for ovarian cancer

reports.text:
Specimens: A) right ovary and fallopian tube; B) left ovary and fallopian tube; C) uterus and cervix; D) omentum; E) right pelvic lymph nodes; F) left pelvic lymph nodes; G) para-aortic lymph nodes; H) peritoneal washings.
A) High-grade serous carcinoma (serous cystadenocarcinoma) of the right ovary, 13.4 cm. Capsule ruptured during removal; no tumor on the ovarian surface. Extensive sampling shows no germ cell or sex cord-stromal component. Right fallopian tube without carcinoma.
B) Left ovary and fallopian tube: no carcinoma.
C) Uterus and cervix: no carcinoma; inactive endometrium.
D) Omentum: no carcinoma.
E-G) Lymph nodes: 0 of 16 involved.
H) Washings: negative for malignant cells.
Pathologic stage: FIGO IC1.
reports.conclusion: High-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, FIGO stage IC1 (intraoperative rupture); lymph nodes 0/16; washings negative.

documents.title: Surgical discharge summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY SERVICE
Admitted 11/06/2025, discharged 11/10/2025

Procedure 11/06: exploratory laparotomy, total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy, pelvic and para-aortic lymph node sampling, peritoneal washings. Frozen section of the right ovary: epithelial carcinoma, so full staging was completed. Capsule ruptured during removal. No visible disease remained.

Course: recovered on the ward without complications. Diet advanced, ambulating, pain controlled on oral medication by discharge.

Final pathology (signed 11/12): high-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, FIGO IC1; nodes 0/16, washings negative. No germ cell component.

Medications at discharge: sertraline 50 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily; short course of oral analgesics. Estradiol/norethindrone discontinued.
Allergies: latex, sulfonamides.

Follow-up: gynecologic oncology clinic 11/20 to plan adjuvant chemotherapy; genetics referral.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology post-operative visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - POST-OP VISIT
Date of service: 11/20/2025

Two weeks out. Incision healing well, eating, walking a mile a day. AFP and beta-hCG today both within the reference range.

Pathology reviewed together: high-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, stage IC1 from rupture at surgery. Because of the high grade and the rupture, I recommend six cycles of adjuvant carboplatin (AUC 6) and paclitaxel (175 mg/m2) every 21 days, first cycle 12/03. Reviewed hair loss, neuropathy, fatigue, infection and blood count risks. Germline genetic panel sent today through our genetics counselor.

We also discussed hormone replacement: she is now surgically menopausal on top of POI. We will hold it through chemotherapy and revisit at the end of treatment.

Allergies: latex, sulfa.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seeing her after ovarian cancer surgery and the first chemo cycle.

Timeline: right ovarian mass found by gyn 10/22, staging CT without spread, laparotomy with TAH/BSO and staging 11/6. High-grade serous carcinoma, stage IC1, nodes negative. Carboplatin/paclitaxel x6 started 12/3, cycles every 3 weeks through March. HRT stopped at surgery; gyn onc to revisit after chemo. Genetics panel pending.

Since cycle 1: tired for 4-5 days, some nausea managed with the cancer center's plan, eating smaller amounts more often. Hair starting to thin, has a scarf. Mood: frightened at diagnosis, steadier now that there is a plan. Not restricting; she is mindful that low appetite and weight loss could pull her back toward old patterns and has reconnected with her former therapist. Partner and mother sharing childcare. Taking leave from teaching through spring.

Exam: thin, tired-appearing. Midline incision well healed. Abdomen soft, nontender. Lungs clear, RRR. No edema. Affect appropriate.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Ovarian cancer, high-grade serous, IC1 - on adjuvant chemo with gyn onc. Lists updated.
2. MDD - stable, continue sertraline 50. Low threshold to increase if mood dips during treatment; she'll message.
3. AN in remission - weight down a little since surgery, eating; will watch weights.
4. POI/surgical menopause - HRT on hold per gyn onc.
Flu and COVID done in September. No Pap needed going forward after hysterectomy for this indication; will confirm surveillance plan with gyn onc.
RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Genetic counseling result letter
documents.author: genetics
documents.body:
CANCER GENETICS PROGRAM - RESULT LETTER
Result date: 12/29/2025

Indication: high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma at 28; family history of breast cancer (mother, 51), ovarian cancer (maternal grandmother, 47), and a sister with a known BRCA1 pathogenic variant.

Test: hereditary cancer multigene panel, sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis, including BRCA1 and BRCA2.

Result: NEGATIVE. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants detected. Specifically, she did not inherit her sister's BRCA1 variant.

Interpretation: her ovarian cancer does not appear to be due to the family's BRCA1 variant. Treatment and surveillance follow the standard approach for her cancer. Her breast screening should still reflect her family history; we will send recommendations to her primary care physician at the appropriate age.

Reviewed with the patient by phone on 12/29/2025.

Genetic Counselor, Cancer Genetics Program

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Last chemo cycle is tomorrow. Fatigue as before, worst the week after each cycle. Nausea controlled. CA-125 down to 18 in February per gyn onc. Genetics negative, which she found a relief for her child's sake and complicated for her sister's.

Mood holding up, PHQ-9 4. Seeing her therapist every other week. Eating three small meals plus snacks, weight steady since December. Teaching one adult class a week on good weeks.

Meds: sertraline 50 daily, vitamin D3 2000 units; finishing carboplatin/paclitaxel at the cancer center. HRT on hold.

Exam: thin, alopecia, well-appearing otherwise. Lungs clear, RRR. Abdomen soft, incision healed. No edema. Affect bright today.

A/P
1. High-grade serous ovarian ca IC1 - final cycle tomorrow, then CT and surveillance with gyn onc.
2. MDD - stable, continue sertraline.
3. AN in remission - stable weight, good support.
4. Surgical menopause/POI - HRT decision with gyn onc after treatment.
RTC in about 6 months, sooner if needed.

documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - END OF TREATMENT
Date of service: 04/21/2026

Completed six cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel, last on 03/18. Energy improving.

CT chest/abdomen/pelvis today: no evidence of disease. CA-125 11 U/mL.

Hormone replacement: for a young woman with primary ovarian insufficiency now surgically menopausal after an early-stage serous cancer, the benefits to bone, heart and quality of life outweigh the risks in our view. Started estradiol 1 mg daily (no progestin needed after hysterectomy).

Surveillance: visit with exam and CA-125 every 3 months for the first two years; imaging as symptoms or markers dictate.

Current medications: estradiol 1 mg daily; sertraline 50 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

Gynecologic Oncology
